newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Jiangxi Copper seen in US$200 mln IPO-paper.
newsitem.headline: China Jiangxi Copper seen in US$200 mln IPO-paper.

text.p: China copper producer Jiangxi Copper plans to raise US$200 million through a share flotation in Hong Kong, the South China Morning Post reported on Monday.
The daily quoting Jiangxi Copper's president He Changming as saying proceeds would be used to boost output by about 40 percent and to reduce debts level to 50 percent from 60 percent.
It gave no further details on the offering.
The report said Hong Kong-listed property concern Silver Grant International Industries Ltd had taken a substantial stake as a strategic investment in Jiangxi Copper through a joint venture.
Silver Grant officials were not immediately available for comment.

The Morning Post said Silver Grant and Jiangxi Copper are both controlled by China National Non-ferrous Metals Industry Corp, which headed by Wu Jianchang, son-in-law of Chinese Patriarch Deng Xiaoping.
A South Korean conglomerate and a Japanese firm have also approached Jiangxi Copper for a 10 percent stake, it said.

The daily also quoting senior sources in Beijing as saying Jiangxi Copper was one of the fourth batch of mainland companies already approached by Beijing's securities regulator, the China Securities Regulatory Commission, for overseas listing and was awaiting final approval from State Council. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6370
